text:
Nick Suzuki is coming off a 101-point season and a Selke Trophy, and he's played only 14 of Montreal's games this fall, with reports that he's still been playing through an injury. When he's in, he's what the Canadiens built around: 17 points, 20:54 a night, and the Habs take 55% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, 5.5 points better than without him.

Some of the scoring is running hot. He has 8 goals on 5.2 expected, shooting 22% against 16% last season, and Montreal has scored 7.4 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. Expect the goals to slow even if the play doesn't. His talent range by our numbers still projects about 91 points over a full season.

The rest is the player he's always been. Evolving-Hockey had him 4th among all forwards in wins above replacement last season, facing the other team's best almost every night, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him in the 89th percentile for setting up shots. The comparison our model finds: Evgeni Malkin. The thing to watch is whether he's fully healthy.
